$comment: Inventory of every externally-versioned pin this repository writes down by hand.
This file is DATA. `scripts/upstream-versions.py` is the only reader; it must never
grow a branch per pin. Adding a pin is an entry here, not a code change.
One entry = one LOGICAL decision, however many files it is written in. The `cue`
toolchain version is one entry with three sources (18 workflow inputs, the devcontainer
installer, the CMP Dockerfile ARG) because bumping it is one decision -- and because a
single entry is what makes the reader able to report DRIFT when the copies disagree.
FIRST-PARTY VERSIONS ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT. platform-stack/cue/component_*.cue for
our own components, argocd-cue-cmp/version.cue, operator/charts/*/Chart.yaml and
platform-stack/cue/platform.cue `currentVersion` are moved by the release workflows
(platform-stack-publish.yml, release-operator.yml, argocd-cue-cmp-publish.yml,
release-backup-runner.yml). They have no upstream to ask, and a watcher that listed
them would be reporting our own release cadence back at us.
FIELDS
id        stable key; used by --only and by the report.
class     grouping for the report and for the test-gap section.
title     human name.
read      how to get the CURRENT value out of the tree. kind:
regex   -- sources[] of {files (git-ls-files glob), pattern}. Group 1 is
the version. Every source must match at least once or the
entry reports UNREADABLE; a pattern that quietly stops
matching is the failure mode this rule exists to prevent.
json    -- file + dotted path (flake.lock).
command -- argv + cwd + pattern; for package-manager aggregates, where
the native tool is a better reader than anything we would write.
upstream  where to ask for the newest value. kind: helm | oci-helm | github-release |
github-branch | docker-hub | crates-io | http-text | none.
compare   numeric -- compare the digit-runs of both strings, newest wins.
major   -- report only when the leading number increases (for `@v4`-style
refs that float within their major on purpose).
minor   -- report only when (major, minor) increases, for pins written as a
minor (`1.98`, `1.4`) whose patch floats on purpose. Under
`numeric` every patch release would read as BEHIND.
none    -- floating by design or not semver-comparable; never reported as
behind. Requires `note` saying why.
gate      Stage 2. What to run against the CANDIDATE version, and what a green
actually proves. null requires `gateGap` -- the reason no cluster-free gate
exists. The report prints `proves` beside every pass, so a green can never
read as more than it is.
note      anything a triager needs that is not obvious from the row.
`{major}` in an upstream field is replaced by the leading number of the in-tree value
("the newest 24.x"). Derived rather than written so the entry follows the tree when
it moves to a new major instead of silently reporting it as ahead of upstream.
GITHUB ACTIONS are pinned by commit SHA with the release as a trailing comment
(`uses: owner/repo@<40-hex> # vX.Y.Z`; scripts/check-workflows.sh enforces the shape,
one SHA per action, one comment per SHA, and with --remote that the comment IS that
commit). Their entries therefore read the COMMENT, never the ref, and compare it
`numeric`: a SHA freezes the patch stream too, so a new release of any size reaches
this repository only when this report says so.

pins.title: nixpkgs (flake input)
pins.gateGap: A `nix flake update` moves the whole tool-belt at once (cue, helm, kubectl, mkdocs-material, ...). The gate that matters is `just docs-check`, whose byte-comparison is protected by NO pin on mkdocs-material -- so a flake update can silently change the docs toolchain. Running it here would need nix in the watch job and would still not attribute a failure to an input. Bump it in a PR and let crd-check.yml + docs.yml judge.
pins.note: flake.nix pins a BRANCH, not a tag, so there is no version to compare -- only lock staleness. crd-check.yml is the only workflow with flake.nix/flake.lock in its pull_request paths.

pins.title: flake-utils (flake input)
pins.gateGap: Same as nixpkgs: no per-input gate exists.
pins.note: Branch ref; staleness only.

pins.title: cue (CLI)

gate.proves: the repo's CUE still formats and vets under the candidate cue (scripts/lint-cue.sh + a platform-stack vet). CUE is the config language here, so this is the gate that actually matters for this pin. It does NOT cover crdgen's byte-comparison, which needs cargo.

pins.note: ONE decision written in 20 places. The Dockerfile ARG is the one that reaches clusters (the Argo CD CMP sidecar evaluates user manifests with it), so a cue bump is a cue-cmp release, not just a CI change.

pins.title: helm (CLI)

gate.proves: the platform-stack umbrella chart still renders and passes `helm lint` under the candidate helm.

pins.note: ONE decision, twelve places. Reconciled UPWARD on 2026-09-22: the v3.16.2/v3.16.4 drift this entry was written to catch was the smaller problem, because helm's support window is n-3 and a 3.16 binary (client-go 0.31) sat outside it for the 1.36.x the k3s stable channel runs. HELM 4 WAS ATTEMPTED THE SAME DAY AND REVERTED -- see the blocker below, and note that every STATIC risk cleared: the chart renders and lints under 4.3.0, helm push emits the same ^Digest: line platform-stack-publish.yml scrapes with a byte-identical digest, bare --wait still parses, and `helm template` of the argo-cd chart with our loader values is semantically IDENTICAL under 3.22.0 and 4.3.0. The Kubernetes window did not change either: both are built against client-go v0.37.0, so the 3.16 move is what closed that gap. WHAT STOPPED IT was the gitops walk, not a static check. Helm 4 makes bare --wait mean the kstatus `watcher` strategy instead of helm 3 legacy readiness, so cluster-bootstrap waits for strictly more and runs ~45% longer (5m27 vs 3m43, same microVM, back to back). That slowdown lets the platform overlay reconcile its 256Mi repo-server limit into place before the walk's assertions, and the repo-server then OOMKills on a cold cluster -- WI-370. Helm 4 does not cause that bug, it changes the schedule enough to reach it. Blocked on WI-370 (WI-368). NOTE this pin governs CI ONLY: cli-core/src/tools.rs checks the user's helm for PRESENCE with no version floor, so a user already on helm 4 pays that bootstrap slowdown today, undetected (WI-369).

pins.title: kubectl (CLI)
pins.gateGap: kubectl is only exercised against a live apiserver. Every workflow that installs it (nightly.yml, e2e-k3d.yml, the seven e2e-*-nightly.yml) needs a cluster -- kind/k3d at minimum, real Hetzner credentials for nightly.yml. A version-watch job must not stand up clusters, so this pin is reported and not tested.
pins.note: Must move in lockstep with the k8s-openapi `features = ["v1_31"]` flag in BOTH Cargo workspaces (cli/Cargo.toml:69, operator/Cargo.toml:46). Nothing links them; this note is the link.

pins.title: kind
pins.gateGap: Out of scope for a WATCH job, which must not stand up clusters on a schedule -- but not ungateable: `just crd-validate` (scripts/validate-crds.sh) creates an ephemeral kind cluster, honours APPRAFTER_KIND_NODE_IMAGE, and therefore gates the kind+node-image pair. CLAUDE.md already mandates it for CRD-changing releases. Run it locally on the bump commit. Caveat measured 2026-09-22: kind >= 0.33 mounts /sys/../lib/modules unconditionally and fails with `statfs /lib/modules: no such file or directory` on hosts that have no /lib/modules (some containers and microVMs), independently of the node image -- GitHub's ubuntu-latest runners do have it.
pins.note: Eight copies of the same literal, no variable. `.github/workflows/**` is in no path-filter that would gate a change to them beyond the workflow's own trigger. NOTE this pin is really TWO decisions: until 2026-09-22 no call site passed `--image`, so the kind BINARY silently chose the Kubernetes version of every e2e cluster (v0.24.0 -> k8s v1.31.0, against a production k3s on 1.36.x). The node image is now written down as APPRAFTER_KIND_NODE_IMAGE in e2e/lib.sh (with its own default in scripts/validate-crds.sh and e2e/jetstream-nack-shape-check.sh, neither of which sources lib.sh) and MUST move together with this pin -- kind supports a node image only with the release that ships it.

pins.title: yq
pins.gateGap: Only used inside two nightly e2e walks that need a cluster.
pins.note: e2e-pg-nightly.yml:106 and e2e-env-and-secrets-nightly.yml:107.

pins.title: just
pins.gateGap: `just` is a command runner; the thing to test is every recipe, i.e. the whole CI matrix. A watch job cannot do that honestly.
pins.note: e2e-k3d.yml:202. Upstream tags carry no `v` prefix, so the compare is on digits only.

pins.title: cilium-cli
pins.gateGap: Used only by e2e-networkpolicy-nightly.yml, which needs kind + real Cilium (and a rootful runtime -- rootless podman's 8 MB memlock cap kills cilium-agent).
pins.note: Must stay compatible with the pinned Cilium chart version, not merely be newest.

pins.title: hubble
pins.gateGap: Same as cilium-cli.
pins.note: Tracks the Cilium minor by convention (v1.16.x beside chart 1.16.5).

pins.title: k3d (devcontainer)
pins.gateGap: Cluster tool; same rule as kind.
pins.note: .devcontainer/** is in no workflow's paths: filter, so nothing in CI has ever run this file.

pins.title: cosign (devcontainer)
pins.gateGap: Signing tool; verifying a bump means signing and verifying a real artefact against the real transparency log, which belongs in the publish workflows, not here.
pins.note: CI uses sigstore/cosign-installer@v3 instead, which floats -- so this devcontainer pin and CI can disagree without anyone noticing.

pins.title: alpine (base image)
pins.gateGap: Building the images is the gate, and only one of the ten Dockerfiles in this tree is built on a PR (argocd-cue-cmp-check.yml:71). Wiring a build into the watch job would duplicate that workflow; the honest move is to add pull_request builds for the other images, which is a CI change of its own.
pins.note: Both copies are on the same minor since 2026-09-22 (the CMP sidecar was on 3.20 and the backup runner on 3.21 until then). The backup runner's tag also CHOOSES its restic: see the `restic` entry, whose build-time assertion fails when a bump here would move the restic minor.

pins.title: restic minor (backup runner image)
pins.gateGap: Moving the minor needs an Alpine tag that packages it, which neither a build-arg nor a watch job can supply. On the bump commit the image build is the first gate (its RESTIC_MINOR assertion fails when the tag ships another minor), and e2e/backup-s3-sequential-kind.sh -- a local two-cluster kind walk against in-cluster MinIO, run by no workflow -- is the one that exercises restic itself.
pins.note: RESTIC_MINOR does not choose restic. The runtime stage's `alpine:` tag does (`apk add restic`), and the build only ASSERTS that the minor it got is this one, failing loudly otherwise. So BEHIND here means a newer restic minor exists upstream, not that the runner can take it: the move is an Alpine tag that packages it (on 2026-09-22 alpine 3.24 ships 0.18.1, edge 0.19.1), a read of the restic changelog for repository-format and S3 behaviour changes, then RESTIC_MINOR and the tag in one commit. The tag itself is image-alpine's row.

pins.title: rust builder image
pins.gateGap: A full cargo-chef release build of an operator image is ~10 minutes and is what release-operator.yml already does after merge. Doing it three times a week to answer `is rust 1.9x fine` is the wrong shape -- bump it in a PR.
pins.note: Three copies of the same builder tag; they have never drifted, and this entry is what would catch it if they did.

pins.title: cargo-chef (build ARG)
pins.gateGap: Same as the rust builder: the gate is the image build.
pins.note: A Dockerfile ARG, so `docker build --build-arg` can test a candidate without editing the tree. The operator images download the prebuilt release binary; the backup runner compiles the same version from crates.io (`cargo install --locked --version`).

pins.title: node LTS major (Backstage host + landing CMS base images, mise.toml)
pins.gateGap: The build is the gate. landing/cms/Dockerfile is built only by release-landing.yml, after a landing/** change reaches master; the Backstage host Dockerfile is a template for an app @backstage/create-app scaffolds, and no workflow builds it. Build both locally on the bump commit.
pins.note: Node is the ONE tool pinned to its MAJOR rather than a minor (owner decision 2026-09-22): Node ships every fix, security releases included (24.13.0 and 24.17.0 were new minors), on the newest minor of an LTS line and never patches an older minor, so a minor pin is an exact pin in practice (24.12 received 0 of the 35 CVE fixes after 24.12.0, and Docker Hub stops rebuilding a minor tag once the next ships). The patterns accept ONLY a bare major, so a minor slipping back into a FROM line or mise.toml reads UNREADABLE instead of passing. Reads the leading number and asks nodejs.org's release index for the newest LTS line (the first entry carrying an `lts` codename; the index is ordered newest first), so an odd Current major, or an even one before it enters LTS, is never reported -- Backstage supports exactly two adjacent LTS majors (`engines.node` in its create-app template).

pins.title: oven/bun major (landing + template builders)
pins.gateGap: The gate is `bun run build` inside the image, which landing-preview-build.yml already performs on the landing side.
pins.note: The MAJOR half of the bun pin, read as the leading number of each builder FROM and compared with the newest major published as an image in the two flavours the tree uses (alpine for the landing builders, debian for the scaffolded template). The minor half is mise-bun, which reads the same FROM lines against bun's GitHub releases. The two never disagree: a new 1.x minor is BEHIND on mise-bun only; a new major is BEHIND on both.

pins.title: caddy (landing + docs static runtime)
pins.gateGap: The gate is the site smoke (scripts/landing-site-smoke.sh, scripts/docs-site-smoke.sh), which probes a deployed site rather than a candidate image.
pins.note: Pinned to a minor with the patch floating, like every base image here, and this is the only row for it: the upstream is the newest `<major>.<minor>-alpine` tag across all majors, so both a new minor and a new major read as BEHIND.

pins.multipleValuesOk: Two different distroless images (static for the Rust binaries, nodejs20 for the template), not two values of one pin.
pins.title: gcr.io/distroless runtimes
pins.gateGap: No version to test; the images are rebuilt continuously under the same tag.
pins.note: distroless publishes no semver tags -- `:nonroot` is a moving tag and the version information is the Debian base (debian12) and, for the template, the node major (nodejs20). Both are human decisions; this row exists so they are at least visible. nodejs20 is the one worth revisiting.

pins.title: actions/checkout
pins.gateGap: An action bump can only be tested by running the workflows that use it. That is a pull request, not a script -- and it is the one class where opening a PR really is the right tool.
pins.note: 47 uses -- the most-used action in the tree. The count is prose, not something the watcher computes, so re-derive it rather than trusting it: grep -c 'uses: actions/checkout@' .github/workflows/*.yml

pins.gateGap: See actions/checkout.
pins.note: The action only installs cue; the cue VERSION is its `version:` input, which is tool-cue.

pins.title: dtolnay/rust-toolchain
pins.gateGap: See actions/checkout.
pins.note: Publishes no releases: a branch per toolchain channel (`stable`, `1.98`, ...) plus `master`, and one tag, `v1`, which followed `master` when this was pinned (2026-09-22) -- hence the `# v1` comment. The old `@stable` was a BRANCH ref that also chose the toolchain; at a commit the toolchain is the required `toolchain:` input, tracked by rust-toolchain-minor. Nothing to compare: to refresh, pin the current `master` commit and run scripts/check-workflows.sh --remote, which fails if `v1` has moved on.

It runs in release-docs.yml, which holds `packages: write`.

Keep full-version comments here. The cosign binary itself is the `cosign-release:` input (v2.4.1, deliberately held below the v3 this action defaults to).

pins.note: Carries the channel-tag publish path (ADR 0041).

pins.note: One of the two Conventional Commits enforcement points (the other is scripts/check-commit-msg.sh).

pins.gateGap: See actions/checkout.

pins.title: taiki-e/install-action
pins.gateGap: See actions/checkout.
pins.note: Installs cargo-deny for test.yml. Releases several times a week, mostly to refresh its tool manifest, so expect this row BEHIND most weeks. That is not noise: the pinned commit also fixes WHICH cargo-deny gets installed, and an old cargo-deny can stop parsing a newer advisory database.

pins.title: Rust toolchain minor (CI, builder images, mise, cli/)
pins.gateGap: A Rust minor is proven by the whole cargo test + clippy matrix under the candidate, i.e. test.yml and lint.yml on a pull request that moves every copy at once. A watch job cannot run that honestly.
pins.note: One decision, four surfaces: CI's dtolnay/rust-toolchain `toolchain:` input, the rust:<minor>-alpine builder images, mise.toml, and cli/rust-toolchain.toml. The last OVERRIDES the first inside cli/ (rustup: toolchain file beats `rustup default`), so a `stable` there silently un-pins every cli/ job in CI, release-cli.yml included -- and the release matrix's cross target is installed for the pinned toolchain only. Minor pinned, patch floats. The flake's nixpkgs rustc is not written in the tree and is not read here (1.95 at the locked rev).

pins.title: bun minor (mise.toml mirrors the builder images)
pins.gateGap: Same as image-bun: `bun run build` inside the image, which landing-preview-build.yml performs.
pins.note: Reads the minor out of every oven/bun FROM line as well as mise.toml, so a builder bump that forgets mise (or the reverse) is DRIFT. Upstream tags are `bun-vX.Y.Z`; the compare takes the digits. The flake's nixpkgs carries bun 1.3 -- behind this, and not read here.

pins.title: just minor (mise.toml mirrors the flake's nixpkgs)
pins.gateGap: Same as tool-just: the thing to test is every recipe.
pins.note: Not compared: the authority is the just in the flake-locked nixpkgs (1.51 at the nixos-26.05 rev), which moves only with flake.lock (flake-nixpkgs), not with upstream releases. After a `nix flake update`, re-derive with `nix eval --raw --inputs-from . nixpkgs#just.version`. CI downloads its own just (tool-just, 1.58.0 today), so dev and CI run different just minors until the flake's release branch catches up.

pins.title: go minor (mise.toml mirrors the flake's nixpkgs)
pins.gateGap: Nothing in this repository builds Go, so there is nothing to run.
pins.note: Not compared, for the reason mise-just gives: the value is the go in the flake-locked nixpkgs (1.26 at the nixos-26.05 rev; `nix eval --raw --inputs-from . nixpkgs#go.version`). flake.nix's devShell does not ship go at all, and no Go code is tracked -- mise.toml keeps it for plugin work.

pins.title: rsa (held)
pins.gateGap: Nothing to gate: the pin cannot move. See heldReason.
pins.heldReason: ON the newest stable and stuck. 0.10 has been in RC since 2025 (rc.18, 2026-04-27) and does NOT fix RUSTSEC-2023-0071 -- the advisory's patched list is empty and RustCrypto/RSA#626 is open. The real gate is `pkcs1` 0.8.0 final (RustCrypto/formats#2385, not started), because `from_pkcs1_pem` is a production call at cli/cli-providers/src/cert.rs:89. The advisory is NOT reachable here: the only production RsaPrivateKey use is cert.rs:67, to_public_key() + compare, and every .decrypt() is #[cfg(test)]. The algorithm is not ours to pick either -- RSA-OAEP is in the type signature of sealed-secrets' own Unseal(). Tracked as an explicit ignore in deny.toml. NOTE removing rsa alone would NOT unify the RustCrypto generation: `age` holds digest 0.10 / rand_core 0.6 independently -- see crate-age.
pins.note: Per-crate entry because the cargo AGGREGATE below reports a COUNT and cannot name a crate, and because a `behind latest` check reports nothing for a crate that is already on latest.

pins.title: serde_yaml (held -- archived)
pins.gateGap: Nothing to gate: the crate is archived, so there is no candidate version to try.
pins.heldReason: ARCHIVED. The newest published version is literally named `0.9.34+deprecated` (2024-03-25); dtolnay deprecated and archived the crate. cargo-deny does NOT catch this one -- there is no RUSTSEC advisory for it -- so without this entry it is invisible to every gate in the tree while reading as perfectly up to date. Successors exist (serde_yaml_ng, serde_norway, serde_yml) but differ in YAML 1.1/1.2 edge-case behaviour, and this repo parses YAML that USERS write, so the swap is a judged product decision rather than a rename. Tracked as WI-367.
pins.note: A workspace dependency in BOTH Cargo workspaces; used in cli-core, docsgen and the platform-stack tooling.

pins.title: age (held -- holds the old RustCrypto generation)
pins.gateGap: Nothing to gate while it is on latest; the blocker is upstream's own dependency choice.
pins.heldReason: On the newest release and still pinning the OLD RustCrypto generation -- digest 0.10, generic-array 0.14, rand_core 0.6 -- independently of the rsa crate. Listed because the obvious conclusion from the rsa entry ("remove rsa and the generation unifies") is WRONG: both hold it, so any plan to move cli/backup-core onto sha2 0.11 / rand 0.9 has to clear this one too. Used for the age-encrypted state cache (cli/cli-core/src/secrets.rs).
pins.note: Encrypts the kubeconfig and argocd password cached under ~/.config/apprafter.

pins.title: cargo dependencies (cli/ workspace)
pins.gateGap: `cargo update` only takes semver-COMPATIBLE upgrades, which the lockfile already allows; the count reported here is the semver-INcompatible remainder, and taking those means editing Cargo.toml ranges per crate. That is a judged change, not a mechanical one -- and CLAUDE.md requires Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock to move in the same commit as a version bump.
pins.note: Reported as an aggregate on purpose. cargo has a first-class reader (`cargo update --dry-run`); reimplementing a crates.io walker would produce a worse answer and 300 rows. Requires cargo on PATH and network -- if cargo is missing the entry reports TOOL-MISSING, not zero.

pins.title: cargo dependencies (operator/ workspace)
pins.gateGap: Same as the cli workspace.
pins.note: Separate Cargo workspace -- there is no top-level Cargo.toml, so this genuinely is a second inventory entry and not a duplicate.

pins.title: bun dependencies (landing/)
pins.gateGap: `bun update` + `bun test` is a real gate and landing-content-check.yml already runs the tests -- but taking every available major (biome 1 -> 2, typescript 5 -> 7) is a migration, not a bump. Aggregate-report it; migrate deliberately.
pins.note: `--filter '*'` covers the workspace root plus web/ and cms/. Requires bun on PATH; reports TOOL-MISSING otherwise.

pins.title: bun dependencies (backstage-plugins/)
pins.gateGap: Backstage plugin dependencies move with the Backstage release train, which is a coordinated upgrade rather than a per-package bump.
pins.note: The frontend plugin and examples/templates/bun-http/skeleton are deliberately NOT tracked: the skeleton is a Backstage scaffolder template whose package.json `name` is the literal placeholder ${{ values.name }} and which ships no lockfile, so bumping it silently changes what every scaffolded user project starts from.
